- Second fastest growing company among the top 30 companies in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market by domestic sales between MAT June 2022 and MAT June 2025 (domestic sales CAGR 16.77% vs IPM 9.21%).
- Fastest growing among the top 30 IPM companies by domestic sales between MAT June 2024 and MAT June 2025 (13.58% vs IPM 7.90%).
- Diversified portfolio of 71 brands with 27 'engine' brands contributing 72.34% of domestic sales in MAT June 2025, including market-leading brands Cor, Trazer, Cor9, B-29 and Myoril.

- Increasing chronic and sub-chronic mix, rising from 63.82% (MAT June 2022) to 70.10% (MAT June 2025) of domestic sales.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Therapeutic-area concentration — Women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto and pain management together contributed 62.40% of FY2025 revenue from operations and 65.14% for the three months ended June 30, 2025; underperformance of these areas would materially affect results.
- Brand concentration — 27 'engine' brands contributed 72.34% of domestic sales in MAT June 2025, so performance is dependent on a limited set of key brands.
- Dependence on specialist prescriptions — Specialists and super-specialists contributed 75.75% of prescriptions in MAT June 2025; changes in prescribing behaviour or access to these doctors could affect sales.
- Pure Offer for Sale — The Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer; all proceeds go to the Selling Shareholders.
- Reliance on third-party industry data — Industry and market positioning claims rely on the CRISIL Intelligence Report commissioned and paid for by the Company, and reliance on such information is subject to inherent risks.
- Non-GAAP measures — The RHP includes non-Ind AS financial measures that are not standardized and may not be comparable with those presented by other companies.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Company has pursued backward integration in manufacturing and R&D through its investment in La Chandra Pharmalab Private Limited, which operates an EU GMP and WHO GMP-certified hormone active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facility in Banaskantha, Gujarat; following the investment, La Chandra develops specified APIs and supplies hormone APIs to the Company under a right of first refusal. The Company also operates two owned formulation manufacturing facilities (Bhayla, Gujarat and Solan, Himachal Pradesh) with owned-manufacturing revenue of 62.75% (three months ended June 30, 2025), 64.01% (FY25), 64.52% (FY24) and 62.02% (FY23) of total revenue from operations, and is commissioning a hormone manufacturing facility in Gujarat expected to start in Q1 FY2027. Distribution is supported by 22 carrying and forwarding (C&F) setups and over 2,000 distributors across India, with a field force of 2,671 medical representatives across 22 states as of June 30, 2025.

objects.purpose: Offer for Sale of Equity Shares by the Selling Shareholders and to achieve the benefits of listing the Equity Shares on the Stock Exchanges; the Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer, which will be received by the Selling Shareholders in proportion to the Offered Shares sold

orders_not_placed.note: Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale; the Company will not receive any proceeds and no funds are deployed towards capital expenditure, so no machinery orders are applicable. No monitoring agency is required to be appointed for the Offer.

project.timeline: Not applicable - the Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale with no fresh issue and no defined capex project; the Company will not receive any proceeds and no funds are deployed towards any project, so there is no means-of-finance / deployment schedule

overview.business_model: The Company develops, manufactures and markets a diversified portfolio of branded pharmaceutical formulations (71 brands as of June 30, 2025) across therapeutic areas such as women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto, pain management and urology, selling primarily in the domestic Indian market through a pan-India sales and marketing network supported by a field force of medical representatives targeting specialist doctors in urban and semi-urban areas.

employee_strength.note: Total employee headcount is not stated in this extract; the DRHP notes a growing field force of 2,671 medical representatives (in the MAT June 2025 context).

genesis.founding_story: Originally incorporated as 'CORONA Remedies Private Limited', a private limited company under the Companies Act, 1956, pursuant to a certificate of incorporation dated August 27, 2004 issued by the Assistant Registrar of Companies, Gujarat at Dadra and Nagar Haveli. The Company was converted into a public limited company pursuant to a special resolution passed by Shareholders on October 24, 2024 and renamed 'CORONA Remedies Limited', with a fresh certificate of incorporation upon conversion issued by the RoC, Central Processing Centre, Manesar, Haryana on December 16, 2024.

milestones.event: Launch of first division, later named as 'Pioneer' division
Commencement of production at the first manufacturing plant at Solan, Himachal Pradesh

name_history: CORONA Remedies Private Limited -> CORONA Remedies Limited (2024)
overview.one_liner: An India-focused branded pharmaceutical formulation company developing, manufacturing and marketing products across women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto, pain management, urology and other therapeutic areas.
overview.registered_office: CORONA House, C – Mondeal Business Park, Near Gurudwara, S. G. Highway, Thaltej, Ahmedabad 380 059, Gujarat, India
verdict_pointers: Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale aggregating up to ₹6,553.71 million; the Company will not receive any proceeds, which go to the Selling Shareholders.
Employee Reservation Portion of up to ₹58.50 million forms part of the Offer.
Per CRISIL Intelligence Report, ranked the second fastest growing among the top 30 companies in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market by domestic sales between MAT June 2022 and MAT June 2025.
Market rank improved from 37th (MAT June 2022) to 29th largest pharmaceutical company in India (MAT June 2025) per CRISIL.
See 'Capital Structure' (p.104), 'Objects of the Offer' (p.123) and 'The Offer' (p.86) for offer and capital detail.

compliance_legal.detail: Many trademarks are pending, opposed, objected, refused or abandoned; inability to obtain/protect trademarks could hurt the business.
compliance_legal.evidence: As of June 30, 2025, portfolio of 71 brands with 194 registered trademarks, 29 pending applications and 67 opposed/objected/refused/abandoned trademarks. Among top 27 brands, 7 brands' trademarks are pending/opposed/objected (Cortel, Argihope, Dosin, Evtab, Alkashot, Tamdosin, Mac). Four trademarks (Oil Control, CF ZIP, CF ZED) lapsed on non-renewal.
compliance_legal.title: Trademark registration gaps and disputes

compliance_legal.detail: The company must obtain and renew numerous licenses and approvals; failure could adversely affect operations. Certain approvals have been applied for but not received.
compliance_legal.evidence: Regulators include State FDA, Ministry of Environment, MoHFW, Ministry of Ayush, DCGI, CDSCO and Gujarat State Drugs Controller. Four material approvals applied for but not received (Solan facility) as of the RHP date.
compliance_legal.title: Obtaining/maintaining/renewing statutory and regulatory licenses

compliance_legal.detail: Facilities are subject to regulatory inspections; future non-compliance could trigger regulatory action.
compliance_legal.evidence: 6 inspections/audits during the past three Financial Years and Q1 FY2026. CDSCO audit of Bhayla facility (October 10–11, 2024) yielded 6 procedural observations. No critical adverse observations received.
compliance_legal.title: Periodic inspections/audits of manufacturing units

financial_valuation.detail: The Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale; the company will not receive any proceeds.
financial_valuation.evidence: Entire proceeds (net of expenses) go to the Selling Shareholders; company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer.
financial_valuation.title: No proceeds to the company (Offer for Sale)

financial_valuation.detail: The business requires significant capex, including for a third manufacturing facility; insufficient cash flows or inability to raise capital could hurt results.
financial_valuation.evidence: Total capital additions ₹210.77 million (6.09% of revenue) Q1 FY2026, ₹900.50 million (7.53%) FY2025, ₹2,850.38 million (28.10%) FY2024 (including intangibles ₹2,074.71 million from Myoril), ₹943.91 million (10.68%) FY2023.
financial_valuation.title: Significant capital expenditure requirements

financial_valuation.detail: The company incurred losses in the past after changing its distribution model; recurrence could adversely affect results and share price.
financial_valuation.evidence: On December 30, 2021 the model changed from super distributors to C&F agents; the company repurchased the entire stock sold to super distributors as on December 30, 2021, leading to a notional loss in the statement of profit and loss.
financial_valuation.title: History of past losses due to distribution-model change

internal_operational.detail: Women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto and pain management contribute a majority of revenue from operations; underperformance or competition in these areas could adversely affect the business.
internal_operational.evidence: These areas aggregated ₹2,257.26 million (65.14%) for the three months ended June 30, 2025 and ₹7,465.54 million (62.40%) for FY2025; individually FY2025 Women's Healthcare 27.53%, Cardio-diabeto 23.67%, Pain Management 11.21%. Total revenue from operations FY2025 ₹11,964.15 million.
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentration in three therapeutic areas

internal_operational.detail: A core portfolio of 27 engine brands drives most domestic sales; adverse developments affecting them could hurt results.
internal_operational.evidence: 27 engine brands accounted for 72.34% of domestic sales (₹10,334.05 million) for MAT June 2025 (out of ₹14,284.89 million total brand sales). B-29 and Myoril combined market share 17.30% in their Covered Market; B-29 10.55% and Myoril 6.75% of domestic sales MAT June 2025. Myoril acquired from Sanofi in FY2024.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on 27 “engine” brands (esp. B-29 and Myoril)

internal_operational.detail: A significant majority of revenue is derived from operations in India; a fall in Indian demand or failure to expand internationally could adversely affect the business.
internal_operational.evidence: Within-India revenue was 96.34% (₹3,338.54 million) for Q1 FY2026 and 96.33% (₹11,524.56 million) for FY2025; outside-India 3.66% and 3.67% respectively.
internal_operational.title: Geographic concentration of revenue within India

strategy_growth.detail: Intense domestic and international competition; failure to respond could reduce market share and profits.
strategy_growth.evidence: Competitors may have greater financial, manufacturing, R&D and marketing resources; industry is rapidly consolidating; pricing pressure noted.
strategy_growth.title: Highly competitive industry

strategy_growth.detail: Success depends on timely product development and commercialization; failed R&D or products could hurt the business.
strategy_growth.evidence: R&D revenue expenditure 1.76% (₹48.69 million) of total expenses Q1 FY2026 and 1.23% (₹118.10 million) FY2025; R&D capex ₹1.60 million (0.76%) Q1 FY2026 and ₹33.34 million (3.70%) FY2025.
strategy_growth.title: Ability to develop and commercialize products (R&D)

strategy_growth.detail: Industry/market data relies on a commissioned CRISIL Intelligence Report; reliance on such information carries inherent risks.
strategy_growth.evidence: CRISIL Intelligence Report (“Assessment of Global and Indian Pharmaceutical Industry,” November 2025) commissioned and paid for by the company pursuant to a commercial proposal dated January 7, 2025.
strategy_growth.title: Reliance on third-party industry report (CRISIL Intelligence)

concerns_observed: The Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale (up to Rs 6,553.71 million); the Company will receive no proceeds and raises no primary growth capital.
High revenue concentration: 27 engine brands were 72.34% of domestic sales (MAT June 2025), three therapeutic areas ~62% of FY2025 revenue, and West Zone 47.30% of domestic sales.
Distribution depends entirely on C&F agents (no owned distribution network); top five C&F agents contributed 44.35% of FY2025 revenue.
Governance/record concerns: untraceable historical RoC filings and share-transfer records, related-party transactions, and Promoter/Promoter Group control of 72.50% pre-Offer continuing post-Offer.

Trademark gaps (67 opposed/objected/refused/abandoned, 29 pending as of June 30, 2025), a pending patent-infringement suit by Vifor/Emcure, DPCO/NLEM price controls on ~9.76% of domestic sales, and no product liability insurance.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue CAGR ~16.33% FY2023-FY2025 (Rs 8,840.50m to Rs 11,964.15m); ranked 2nd fastest growing among top 30 IPM companies per CRISIL; rank improved 37th to 29th.
PAT grew Rs 849.29m (FY2023) to Rs 1,494.34m (FY2025); RoNW 24.65% FY2025; EBITDA Rs 1,350.30m to Rs 2,459.13m; margins not separately stated in extract.
Total borrowings Rs 626.95m (FY2025), down from Rs 1,341.42m (FY2024, Myoril-funded); CARE A+; Stable / CARE A1 rating; export obligations Rs 296.86m outstanding.
27 engine brands 72.34% of domestic sales; top 3 therapeutic areas ~62% FY2025; West Zone 47.30%; top five C&F agents 44.35% of FY2025 revenue; ~96% domestic.

Board of 8 with 4 independent directors; Promoter/Promoter Group 72.50% pre-Offer; untraceable historical RoC forms and share-transfer records; related-party transactions and interested promoters/lease agreements.

29th largest pharma company in India and 17th in its Covered Market (MAT June 2025); niche 'middle of the pyramid' specialist-focused positioning; competes with far larger listed peers (Abbott India, Mankind, Torrent).

Pending patent-infringement suit (Vifor/Emcure); litigation against Directors/Promoters aggregating Rs 16.98m each; 67 opposed/objected trademarks; 4 Solan-facility approvals applied-for-but-not-received; DPCO price controls; no product liability insurance.
100% Offer for Sale of up to Rs 6,553.71 million; Company receives no proceeds; no fresh issue or primary capital deployment; Employee Reservation Portion up to Rs 58.50 million.

red_flags: Untraceable historical RoC forms (Form 23AC FY2007, Form 66 FY2006, Form 23B FY2008/2010/2011) and share-transfer records; a Form 2 (May 26, 2010) mis-described a bonus issue as a further issue.
Pending patent-infringement plaint by Vifor International and Emcure Pharmaceuticals in the High Court of Delhi.
No product liability insurance maintained despite voluntary product recalls in the past three FYs and Q1 FY2026; fire insurance only at the Bhayla facility.
History of past losses following the December 2021 distribution-model change (repurchase of super-distributor stock caused a notional loss).
strengths_observed: Revenue from operations grew at a ~16.33% CAGR from Rs 8,840.50 million (FY2023) to Rs 11,964.15 million (FY2025), with PAT rising from Rs 849.29 million to Rs 1,494.34 million over the same period.

Per CRISIL Intelligence Report, second fastest growing among the top 30 companies in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market by domestic sales (MAT June 2022 to MAT June 2025); market rank improved from 37th to 29th.
Return on net worth of 24.65% in FY2025 (20.79% FY2023, 18.84% FY2024) alongside relatively low total borrowings of Rs 626.95 million (FY2025) and a CARE A+; Stable / CARE A1 credit rating.

Diversified portfolio of 71 brands across women's healthcare, cardio-diabeto, pain management, urology and other therapeutic areas, with 12 of 27 engine brands ranked in the top five in their categories.
Backward integration in hormone APIs via associate La Chandra Pharmalab (EU GMP / WHO GMP facility) and a new hormone manufacturing facility expected to commence in Q1 FY2027.
